d686f7821e25.tr:
You are a teaching assistant for a machine learning class. Write Python code that runs as is in Google Colab.

[Environment] Use only Colab's default libraries (numpy, pandas, scikit-learn) and ucimlrepo. Print the scikit-learn version on the first line.
[Data] Load the concrete compressive strength data with 〔fetch_ucirepo(id=165) from ucimlrepo〕.
  - Features X: the 8 columns 〔cement, blast-furnace slag, fly ash, water, superplasticizer, coarse aggregate, fine aggregate, age〕 (name them in column order)
  - Target y: 〔compressive strength (MPa)〕 (regression). Check with assert that the target column has not slipped into X.
[Rules]
  1) First split with train_test_split(test_size=0.25, random_state=42), stratified by 3 grades that cut strength at 〔25, 45〕 MPa.
  2) Fit StandardScaler on the training data only; only transform the test data.
  3) Train with LinearRegression(). Do not use arguments removed in my scikit-learn version (normalize, squared, etc.).
[Output] Training and test R², MAE and RMSE, the weight for each feature (coef_) and the intercept, a comparison with DummyRegressor that always answers the mean, and the mean residual for each age range.
[Forbidden] Do not train on the test data or choose features with it. Do not make up data.
[Format] Split the code into cells and put a comment in English above each cell saying what it does. After the code, list 3 things I should check.

Make questions for an introductory linear regression class. The audience is 〔practitioners on the manufacturing floor, not used to formulas〕. Use concrete strength prediction for all examples.
- 5 multiple-choice questions, one each on residuals, least squares, MAE and RMSE, R², and gradient descent (3 options each, with answer explanations)
- 2 questions that expose misconceptions: "If R² is high, the MPa error is small too", "The feature with the largest weight is the cause"
- 1 calculation problem that can be solved by hand: find MAE, RMSE and R² from the actual and predicted strengths of 4 mixes (two decimal places)
Collect the answers separately at the very end.

a40e5b222a08.ko: 오늘부터 질문이 바뀐다. "35MPa를 넘는가?"가 아니라 "이 배합은 몇 MPa인가?"다. 답이 이름표가 아니라 크기가 있는 숫자이므로 회귀다. 회귀팀의 합격선은 매뉴얼 씨가 들고 온 현장 경험식이다. 물-결합재비와 재령만 넣으면 강도를 계산해 주는 오래된 공식이다.
a40e5b222a08.ctx: ⟦오늘부터 질문이 바뀐다. "35MPa를 넘는가?"가 아니라 "이 배합은 몇 MPa인가?"다. 답이 이름표가 아니라 크기가 있는 숫자이므로 회귀다. 회귀팀의 합격선은 매뉴얼 씨가 들고 온 현장 경험식이다. 물-결합재비와 재령만 넣으면 강도를 계산해 주는 오래된 공식이다.⟧
a40e5b222a08.tr: From today, the question changes. Not "Is it over 35 MPa?" but "How many MPa is this mix?" The answer is a number with size, not a label, so this is regression. The Regression Team's hiring bar is the field formula Mr. Manual brought. It is an old formula that calculates strength from just the water–binder ratio and the age.

855983bd84c7.ko: 선형 회귀는 특징마다 가중치를 곱해 더한 값 하나로 강도를 맞힌다. 예측과 실제의 차이(잔차)를 제곱해 모두 더한 값이 가장 작아지는 가중치를 고른다. 이것이 최소제곱이다. 답은 행렬 계산 한 번(정규방정식)으로 나오고, 조금씩 내려가는 경사 하강으로도 같은 곳에 닿는다.
855983bd84c7.ctx: ⟦선형 회귀는 특징마다 가중치를 곱해 더한 값 하나로 강도를 맞힌다. 예측과 실제의 차이(잔차)를 제곱해 모두 더한 값이 가장 작아지는 가중치를 고른다. 이것이 최소제곱이다. 답은 행렬 계산 한 번(정규방정식)으로 나오고, 조금씩 내려가는 경사 하강으로도 같은 곳에 닿는다.⟧
855983bd84c7.tr: Linear regression predicts strength with one value: each feature multiplied by a weight and added up. It picks the weights that make the sum of the squared differences between prediction and reality (residuals) smallest. This is least squares. The answer comes out of one matrix calculation (the normal equation), and gradient descent, stepping down little by little, reaches the same place.

7efb2d88129f.tr: Slope 0, and the height is the mean strength of the training mixes. It is a line that answers only "35.8 MPa on average" to any mix, and this is the regression baseline. R² measures by what percentage the sum of squared residuals is reduced compared with this mean line. So the R² of the mean line is exactly 0. Move the slope and look for the direction where R² becomes greater than 0.

79a10041b53f.ko: 잔차를 그냥 더하면 +와 −가 지워져 엉터리 직선도 합이 0이 된다. 절댓값을 더해도 되지만(그러면 MAE를 줄이는 다른 회귀가 된다), 제곱하면 미분이 깔끔해져 답이 식 하나로 나온다(04장 정규방정식). 대신 큰 잔차를 더 크게 벌하므로 튀는 값 몇 개에 직선이 끌려간다. "잔차 제곱 보기"에서 큰 정사각형이 바로 그 끌어당기는 힘이다.

79a10041b53f.tr: If you just add up the residuals, + and − cancel, and even a nonsense line can sum to 0. You could add absolute values (that gives a different regression that minimizes MAE), but squaring makes the derivative clean, so the answer comes out as one formula (the normal equation in Section 04). In exchange, it punishes big residuals more, so the line gets pulled by a few outliers. In "Show squared residuals," the big squares are exactly that pulling force.

aa4283a51faf.ko: 물-결합재비는 클수록 강도가 낮아져 기울기가 음수다. 시멘트는 양수다. 재령을 고르면 점들이 처음에 가파르게 오르다 눕는 곡선을 그리는데, 직선은 이 모양을 따라가지 못한다. 7일 근처와 365일 근처에서 직선이 점들 위로 지나가고, 28~90일에서는 아래로 지나간다. 이 어긋남이 05장의 "잔차의 무늬"이고, 이 면접의 승부처다.

Pick age and the points draw a curve that rises steeply at first and then levels off, which a straight line cannot follow. Near 7 days and 365 days the line passes above the points, and at 28–90 days it passes below. This mismatch is the "pattern in the residuals" of Section 05, and it decides this interview.

338e0a548291.tr: The first part is Abrams' law, over 100 years old: "more water means weaker." The second part is the ACI 209R correction giving the strength at age t days as a multiple of the 28-day strength. The four numbers (96.5, 7, 4, 0.85) are textbook values, not learned from this data. Exam-paper R² 0.735, MAE 6.72 MPa. Put in the water–cement ratio as in the original formula, and R² collapses to 0.058. The knowledge that slag and fly ash also harden is what saves the formula.

5cb731bf4281.tr: Unregularized linear regression gives exactly the same predictions with standardization. If you write cement in tons instead of kg, the weight just grows 1,000× and the line stays the same (check it in "Change the conditions and look again" in the interview result). There are still two reasons to standardize. ① You can compare weight sizes (Section 06). ② Gradient descent converges much faster (Section 04). From the regularization in 5-3 (Ridge·Lasso) on, standardization changes the score itself. The mean and standard deviation come from the training data only.

The committee's rule is the same: code from an AI is like a candidate's cover letter. Read it, doubt it, run it and check.

19dcac758e11.ko: LinearRegression(normalize=True)는 scikit-learn 1.0에서 예고된 뒤 1.2에서 없어졌다. 표준화가 필요하면 StandardScaler를 따로 쓴다(파이프라인으로 묶으면 편하다). RMSE를 구하던 mean_squared_error(..., squared=False)도 1.4에서 예고된 뒤 1.6에서 없어졌고, 지금은 root_mean_squared_error를 쓴다. 예제 데이터 load_boston은 1.2에서 삭제됐다. AI는 예전 코드를 많이 보고 배웠기 때문에 이 셋을 자주 쓴다. 첫 줄에서 print(sklearn.__version__)로 버전을 찍고, 경고(FutureWarning)를 무시하지 않는다.

RMSE를 구하던 mean_squared_error(..., squared=False)도 1.4에서 예고된 뒤 1.6에서 없어졌고, 지금은 root_mean_squared_error를 쓴다. 예제 데이터 load_boston은 1.2에서 삭제됐다. 5d625ba1ce71.ctx: ⟦MSE는 가중치에 대한 2차식이라 그릇 모양이고 바닥이 하나다. 바닥에서는 기울기가 0이므로, 그 조건을 식으로 쓰면 연립방정식 (XᵀX)β = Xᵀy가 된다. 특징이 8개면 9×9 방정식 하나를 풀면 끝이다. 반복도, 학습률도 필요 없다.⟧
5d625ba1ce71.tr: MSE is a quadratic in the weights, so it is bowl-shaped with a single bottom. At the bottom the gradient is 0, and writing that condition as equations gives the system (XᵀX)β = Xᵀy. With 8 features, you solve one 9×9 system and you are done. No iterations, no learning rate.

90885283c8b0.ko: 특징이 수만 개면 XᵀX가 수만×수만 행렬이 되어 풀기 버겁고, 데이터가 메모리에 다 안 들어가면 XᵀX를 만들 수도 없다. 경사 하강은 데이터를 조금씩 보며 걸어가므로 이럴 때 쓴다. 신경망처럼 바닥을 식으로 풀 수 없는 모델은 경사 하강밖에 없다. 한 걸음의 식은 5-4 로지스틱 회귀와 꼴이 같다. "틀린 만큼 × 특징"의 평균이다.
90885283c8b0.ctx: ⟦특징이 수만 개면 XᵀX가 수만×수만 행렬이 되어 풀기 버겁고, 데이터가 메모리에 다 안 들어가면 XᵀX를 만들 수도 없다. 경사 하강은 데이터를 조금씩 보며 걸어가므로 이럴 때 쓴다. 신경망처럼 바닥을 식으로 풀 수 없는 모델은 경사 하강밖에 없다. 한 걸음의 식은 5-4 로지스틱 회귀와 꼴이 같다. "틀린 만큼 × 특징"의 평균이다.⟧
90885283c8b0.tr: With tens of thousands of features, XᵀX becomes a tens-of-thousands-square matrix that is hard to solve, and if the data does not fit in memory, you cannot even build XᵀX. Gradient descent walks while looking at a little data at a time, so it is used in such cases. For models like neural networks, whose bottom cannot be solved by formula, gradient descent is the only way. The formula for one step has the same form as 5-4 logistic regression: the average of "how wrong × feature."

c9d86554ffd6.tr: R² 0.567 means "it reduced the sum of squared residuals of just saying the mean by 56.7%." You can also read it as explaining a little over half the spread in strength. R² has no unit, which makes it good for comparing with other data, but it does not tell the field "how many MPa off." So always use it with MAE. On the exam paper R² can even be negative, meaning worse than the mean (the degree-4 polynomial in 5-3).

ebe4cbd7bc49.tr: Data and calculations. The practical exam is the UCI Concrete Compressive Strength data, 1,030 mixes; the exam paper is the 258 mixes split with test_size=0.25, stratify=3 strength grades, random_state=42. Mr. Manual's empirical formula, the Regression Team hiring bar, is Abrams' law (f28 = 96.5 / 7^water–binder ratio, textbook constants A = 14,000 psi ≈ 96.5 MPa, B = 7) multiplied by the ACI 209R age correction t / (4 + 0.85t); the formula, originally written with the water–cement ratio, was widened to the water–binder ratio and set for teaching. It is not a standard for real mix design or quality judgment. The numbers in Sections 01·04·05·06 and the interview result are calculated directly in the browser by this page (the normal equation is solved by Gaussian elimination, and the probation replay by gradient descent). They match the Colab results (Section A) to the third decimal place. The 'AI-written code' in Section 03 is a deliberately constructed example collecting common mistakes, not an actual answer from any particular AI service.
